title: Brahma Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: First of the eighteen (VP 3.6.20: 'ādyaṃ sarvapurāṇānām'); told by Lomaharṣaṇa at Naimiṣa.
attribution.scholarly: A compilation with Orissan (Puruṣottama/Konārka) and Godāvarī (Gautamī-māhātmya) layers and borrowed epic material; closing chapters parallel the Mahābhārata's Mokṣadharma.

scholarly.text: compiled c. 10th-13th c. CE with older borrowed material

structure.description: 246 chapters in the critical edition (Schreiner & Söhnen-Thieme); c. 10,000 verses by the traditional count (BhP 12.13.4)

editions.name: Brahmapurāṇa, ed. P. Schreiner & R. Söhnen-Thieme (GRETIL e-text)

notes: Chapters c. 234-245 contain Sāṃkhya-yoga dialogues (e.g. 240.96; 243.20 'ekaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ ca yogaṃ ca yaḥ paśyati sa buddhimān'); chapter checked in the GRETIL e-text of the Brahma Purāṇa (Schreiner & Söhnen-Thieme)
summary: The 'first' Purāṇa: creation, Bhū-maṇḍala and genealogies, the māhātmyas of the Puruṣottama-kṣetra (Purī) and of the Gautamī (Godāvarī) tīrthas, Kṛṣṇa's life, śrāddha and dharma, and closing Sāṃkhya-yoga teachings on liberation.

title: Padma Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Compiled by Vyāsa (Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana) from the one primeval Purāṇa and taught through Romaharṣaṇa and his line. Told of the time when the world was a golden lotus (Matsya 53.14).
attribution.scholarly: Survives in two main recensions - a Bengal recension in five khaṇḍas and a South Indian/Ānandāśrama recension in six khaṇḍas (the Venkateshwara print arranges Sṛṣṭi, Bhūmi, Svarga, Brahma, Pātāla, Uttara and Kriyāyogasāra); many layers of different date.

structure.description: khaṇḍas differing by recension; 55,000 verses by the traditional count (BhP 12.13.4; Matsya 53.14)

notes: Contains the Bhāgavata-māhātmya (Uttarakhaṇḍa; colophon checked in the local e-text), the Gītā-māhātmya, the Śiva Gītā (U06), the classification of the Purāṇas by the three guṇas (Uttarakhaṇḍa; ch. number edition-dependent, often cited as 236.18-21), and the list of ten offences against the name as cited by Gauḍīya authors.
summary: A vast Vaiṣṇava-leaning compendium: creation, tīrthas (Puṣkara and others), vratas (Ekādaśī, Kārttika, Māgha), the glory of the Bhāgavata and the Gītā, Rāma narratives, the worship of the name and of the śālagrāma and tulasī, and the guṇa-classification of the eighteen Purāṇas.

title: Viṣṇu Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Spoken by Parāśara to Maitreya (VP 1.1), the narrative of the Vārāha-kalpa (Matsya 53.16-17); within the eighteen compiled by Vyāsa.
attribution.scholarly: One of the most unified Purāṇas; closely matches the classical five marks; Book 5 parallels the Harivaṃśa.

tradition.text: Parāśara's teaching; Vyāsa's compilation at the end of Dvāpara

scholarly.text: commonly placed in the first half of the 1st millennium CE (estimates vary widely)

structure.description: 6 aṃśas (books), 126 chapters in the common vulgate; c. 23,000 verses by the traditional count (BhP 12.13.4) but c. 6,000-7,000 in the extant text

editions.name: Viṣṇupurāṇa with Viṣṇucittīya and Śrīdhara's Ātmaprakāśa (local e-text, raw_etexts)

notes: Book 6 ch. 6-7: Keśidhvaja teaches Khāṇḍikya yoga; Book 2 ch. 13-16: Bharata and Ṛbhu-Nidāgha. verse number checked in the local e-text of the VP with the Viṣṇucittīya and Ātmaprakāśa commentaries (raw_etexts mAdhva-app)
summary: The model Purāṇa of the five marks: creation from pradhāna and puruṣa as forms of Viṣṇu, Bhū-maṇḍala and the worlds and hells, manvantaras and the Vyāsas, varṇāśrama and śrāddha, the solar and lunar dynasties, Kṛṣṇa's life, the Kali age and the four dissolutions, and the yoga of Keśidhvaja with Viṣṇu as its support.

title: Vāyu Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Proclaimed by Vāyu, the wind god, in the Śveta-kalpa, joined with the glory of Rudra (Matsya 53.18); several lists count it fourth in place of the Śiva Purāṇa (Matsya 53.18; Nārada 1.95).
attribution.scholarly: Regarded by most scholars as among the oldest Purāṇas; it shares a common core with the Brahmāṇḍa (the Kūrma list calls the eighteenth 'Vāyavīya ... named Brahmāṇḍa').

structure.description: four pādas (prakriyā, anuṣaṅga, upodghāta, upasaṃhāra); 24,000 verses by the traditional count (Matsya 53.18)

notes: Contains Pāśupata-yoga chapters, the Gayā-māhātmya (appendix) and śrāddha-kalpa; exact chapter numbers not checked (no local e-text) - low confidence on locators.
summary: An early Śaiva-leaning Purāṇa of the classic type: creation, cosmography, time, manvantaras and genealogies, Pāśupata yoga with its obstacles and powers, śrāddha, and (in an appended portion) the glory of Gayā for the ancestors.

title: Bhāgavata Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Composed by Vyāsa, at Nārada's urging, after the Mahābhārata (BhP 1.5-7); taught by Śuka to Parīkṣit on the Gaṅgā during the king's last seven days; retold by the Sūta (Ugraśravas) at Naimiṣa. Given first by the Lord to Brahmā on the lotus (BhP 12.13.10; 2.9 catuḥślokī).
attribution.scholarly: Usually dated c. 9th-10th c. CE and located in the Tamil south, in the milieu of the Āḻvārs; its style is deliberately archaic. Opponents of the text once alleged authorship by the 13th-c. grammarian Vopadeva (see dsp:which-bhagavata-is-the-mahapurana).

tradition.text: Vyāsa's composition at the beginning of the Kali age; recited by Śuka to Parīkṣit

scholarly.text: c. 9th-10th c. CE (some scholars earlier, 6th-8th c.)

structure.description: 12 skandhas, 335 chapters (with variants), 18,000 verses by its own count (BhP 12.13.9)

editions.name: Gita Press Śrīmad Bhāgavata (local e-text, raw_etexts bhAgavata-purANam/wiki)

notes: Commentaries: Śrīdhara Svāmin's Bhāvārthadīpikā (src:bhavarthadipika), Madhva's Bhāgavata-tātparya-nirṇaya, Vīrarāghava, Vijayadhvaja, Vallabha's Subodhinī, Sanātana's Bṛhad-vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī, Jīva's Krama-sandarbha, Viśvanātha's Sārārthadarśinī (owned by U13-U16 where they create them). Contains the Kapila Gītā (3.25-33) and Uddhava Gītā (11.7-29), which U06 owns. verse number checked in the local e-text (sanskrit/raw_etexts, bhAgavata-purANam/wiki; Gita Press-type numbering)
summary: The foremost Vaiṣṇava Purāṇa: Kṛṣṇa as Bhagavān himself; bhakti as the supreme dharma; the ten marks; creation, avatāras and cosmography (worlds, Bhū-maṇḍala, hells); the stories of Dhruva, Prahlāda, Ajāmila, Gajendra, Jaḍa Bharata and Ṛṣabha; Kṛṣṇa's life in Vraja with the rāsa-līlā and the gopīs' love in separation (Book 10); the Uddhava Gītā on yoga, powers and devotion; the Kali age, the dissolutions and Śuka's final non-dual teaching.

title: Nārada Purāṇa
alt_titles: Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa (so named in the printed colophons)

attribution.tradition: Nārada's teaching of the dharmas of the Bṛhat-kalpa (Matsya 53.23); the four Kumāras (Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatkumāra, Sanātana) instruct Nārada.
attribution.scholarly: The Mahāpurāṇa is distinguished by scholars from a separate Bṛhannāradīya Upapurāṇa, but printed colophons of the Mahāpurāṇa use 'Bṛhannāradīya'.

scholarly.text: late compilation (roughly late 1st to mid 2nd millennium CE)

structure.description: Pūrvabhāga (four pādas, c. 125 chapters) and Uttarabhāga (c. 82 chapters); 25,000 verses by the traditional count

notes: Pūrvabhāga chs. 92-109: a summary-index (anukramaṇī) of all eighteen Purāṇas (the list there counts the Vāyu fourth); following chapters: tithi-vratas for the twelve months; Pūrva 3rd pāda: mantra-śāstra; Uttarabhāga: Ekādaśī/Dvādaśī-māhātmya with Rukmāṅgada and Mohinī, and tīrtha-māhātmyas. chapter checked in the GRETIL/Sansknet e-text of the Nārada Purāṇa
summary: A Vaiṣṇava Purāṇa of dharma and ritual: devotion to Viṣṇu, the Vedāṅgas, mantra-śāstra, the tithi-vratas of the year, the contents of all eighteen Purāṇas, the Ekādaśī vow (with Yama's lament that his realm is emptied by it), and the glories of many tīrthas.

title: Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Mārkaṇḍeya tells Jaimini to go to the four wise birds (sons of Droṇa) in the Vindhya, who answer his questions (MkP 1-3; Matsya 53.25-26).
attribution.scholarly: One of the older Purāṇas, with little sectarian colouring; the Devī Māhātmya (chs. 81-93 in the Venkateshwara/Sansknet numbering, 78-90 in some others) is a separable later insertion.

scholarly.text: core c. 3rd-6th c. CE; Devī Māhātmya c. 5th-6th c. CE

structure.description: c. 134-137 chapters in full editions (the GRETIL/Sansknet e-text has chs. 1-93); 9,000 verses by the traditional count

notes: Chs. 10-15: Sumati ('Jaḍa') on death, the road of Yama and the hells, and Vipaścit; 16-44: Dattātreya's birth and his teaching (through Madālasā's son Alarka) - yoga chs. 39-43; 45-80: creation, time, cosmography and the manvantaras; 81-93: Devī Māhātmya. verse number checked in the GRETIL/Sansknet e-text of the MkP (chs. 1-93; Devī Māhātmya = MkP 81-93 in this numbering)
summary: A Purāṇa of dialogues: the birth, death and after-death journey of beings; the hells; Madālasā's teaching to her sons; Dattātreya's yoga for Alarka (posture, breath, dhāraṇā, obstacles, powers, Oṃ, the signs of death); creation, time and the fourteen manvantaras; and the Devī Māhātmya.

title: Agni Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Spoken by Agni to Vasiṣṭha about the Īśāna-kalpa (Matsya 53.28).
attribution.scholarly: An encyclopedic compilation drawing on Pāñcarātra and Śaiva ritual manuals, poetics, grammar, medicine, polity and archery.

structure.description: 382 chapters (Bibliotheca Indica, R. Mitra) or 383 (Ānandāśrama); 15,400 verses by the traditional count (BhP 12.13.5)

editions.name: Agnipurāṇa, ed. Rajendralal Mitra, Bibliotheca Indica 1870-79 (GRETIL e-text)

notes: Chs. 2-16: the ten avatāras (16: the Buddha as Māyāmoha, then Kalki); 49: images of the ten avatāras; 114-116: Gayā; 370: hells; 371-375: the eight limbs of yoga; 376-379: knowledge of Brahman and non-dual knowledge; 380: Gītāsāra; 381: Yamagītā. chapter checked in the GRETIL e-text of the Agni Purāṇa (R. Mitra, Bibliotheca Indica numbering; other editions differ)
summary: An encyclopedia of Purāṇic knowledge: the avatāras, temple building and image installation, dīkṣā and worship, tīrthas (Gayā), vratas and gifts, astrology, medicine, polity, poetics and grammar, and closing chapters on the hells, the eight limbs of yoga and non-dual knowledge of Brahman.

title: Bhaviṣya Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: The Purāṇa of the future, spoken with the Aghora-kalpa (per the lists).
attribution.scholarly: Heterogeneous: the Brāhma-parvan preserves early material on sun worship and the Maga priests; the Pratisarga-parvan contains passages about second-millennium rulers and other late matter that scholars regard as 18th-19th c. additions; the Uttara-parvan is the Bhaviṣyottara (vrata-kathās).

scholarly.text: layers from the mid 1st millennium CE to the 19th c. CE

structure.description: four parvans in the Venkateshwara print (Brāhma, Madhyama, Pratisarga, Uttara); 14,500 verses by the traditional count

summary: The 'Purāṇa of the future': sun worship and the Magas, dharma and saṃskāras, prophecies of future kings, and (in the Uttara-parvan) the narratives of vows.

title: Brahmavaivarta Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Told by Sāvarṇi to Nārada about the Rathantara-kalpa (per the lists); 18,000 verses.
attribution.scholarly: The extant text is a late Bengal recasting centred on Rādhā and Kṛṣṇa in Goloka; it differs from the text summarised in older lists.

scholarly.text: extant form c. 15th-16th c. CE, Bengal (older core lost)

structure.description: four khaṇḍas: Brahma, Prakṛti, Gaṇapati, Kṛṣṇajanma

summary: Kṛṣṇa as the supreme Person in Goloka with Rādhā as his śakti; Prakṛti's five principal forms (Durgā, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Sāvitrī, Rādhā); Gaṇeśa's birth; Kṛṣṇa's life with a strong Rādhā-centred devotion.

title: Liṅga Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Spoken by Śiva/Nandin in the Agni-kalpa (per the lists); 11,000 verses.
attribution.scholarly: A Śaiva Purāṇa with strong Pāśupata elements and ritual (dāna) chapters.

structure.description: Pūrvabhāga 108 chapters, Uttarabhāga 55 chapters

notes: 1.3: aliṅga and liṅga; 1.7-9: Pāśupata yoga, eight limbs, ten obstacles, six upasargas/siddhis; 1.17-19 (approx.): the appearance of the liṅga of fire; 1.65 and 1.98: thousand names of Śiva; 1.85: pañcākṣara; 1.88: the eight siddhis; 1.91: signs of death; 2.28-45 (approx.): the great gifts and the jīvac-chrāddha; 2.55: Pāśupata yoga. verse number checked in the local e-text of the Liṅga Purāṇa (raw_etexts mAdhva-app)
summary: The Purāṇa of the liṅga: Śiva as the unmanifest (aliṅga) source of the manifest sign (liṅga), the column of fire whose ends Brahmā and Viṣṇu cannot find, Pāśupata yoga and vows, the pañcākṣara, the thousand names of Śiva, the great gifts and the rites for the dead.

title: Varāha Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: The teaching of Varāha (Viṣṇu as the Boar) to the Earth, 24,000 verses by the traditional count.
attribution.scholarly: Extant text much shorter; Vaiṣṇava with Mathurā-māhātmya; includes a Naciketas narrative of the hells.

summary: Varāha's teaching to the Earth: vows (especially the dvādaśī vows), Viṣṇu worship, the glory of Mathurā, and narratives of hell and Yama's realm (a Naciketas episode).

title: Skanda Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Told by Skanda (Kumāra/Ṣaṇmukha); the largest Purāṇa, 81,100 verses by the traditional count (BhP 12.13.7); arranged either in seven khaṇḍas or in six saṃhitās (Sanatkumāra, Sūta, Śaṅkara, Vaiṣṇava, Brāhma, Saura).
attribution.scholarly: The printed Skanda (seven khaṇḍas) is a loose corpus of tīrtha- and vrata-māhātmyas of many dates and regions; a distinct early 'Skandapurāṇa' survives in Nepalese manuscripts, the oldest dated 810 CE (src:skandapurana-early).

scholarly.text: components from c. 8th to 18th c. CE

structure.description: Venkateshwara print: seven khaṇḍas - Māheśvara (Kedāra, Kaumārikā, Aruṇācala), Vaiṣṇava (Veṅkaṭācala, Puruṣottama, Badarikāśrama, Kārttika, Mārgaśīrṣa, Bhāgavata-māhātmya, Vaiśākha, Ayodhyā, Vāsudeva), Brahma (Setu, Dharmāraṇya, Brahmottara), Kāśī, Āvantya (incl. Revā), Nāgara, Prabhāsa

notes: Kāśī Khaṇḍa 6.28-45 (SkP 4.1.6): the inner (mānasa) tīrthas. The Guru Gītā claims a Skanda origin (U06). verse number checked in the local e-text of the Skanda Purāṇa (raw_etexts skanda-purANam)
summary: The great compendium of sacred places and times: māhātmyas of Kedāra, Aruṇācala, Veṅkaṭācala, Puruṣottama, Badarī, Ayodhyā, Setu, Kāśī, Avanti and the Narmadā, Prabhāsa and Dvārakā; the months and vows; and teaching on the inner meaning of pilgrimage.

title: Vāmana Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: The narrative of Vāmana (Trivikrama), 10,000 verses by the traditional count.
attribution.scholarly: Extant text combines Vaiṣṇava and Śaiva material, with Kurukṣetra/Sarasvatī māhātmyas.

summary: The dwarf avatāra and Bali; the glory of Kurukṣetra and the Sarasvatī; Śiva and Pārvatī narratives; vows.

title: Kūrma Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Spoken by Viṣṇu as the Tortoise (Kūrma) to Indradyumna and the sages; the fifteenth Purāṇa, in four saṃhitās (Brāhmī, Bhāgavatī, Saurī, Vaiṣṇavī) of which the Brāhmī (6,000 verses) is this text (KūP 1.1.21-23).
attribution.scholarly: A Pāśupata-Śaiva redaction of an originally Vaiṣṇava Purāṇa; teaches the identity of Śiva and Viṣṇu.

structure.description: Pūrvabhāga c. 51-53 chapters, Uparibhāga c. 44-46 chapters; 17,000 verses by BhP 12.13.8, 6,000 in the Brāhmī saṃhitā by its own count

notes: Uparibhāga 1-11 is the Īśvara Gītā (src:isvara-gita, U06), followed by the Vyāsa Gītā (chapter range edition-dependent). verse number checked in the local e-text of the Kūrma Purāṇa (raw_etexts mAdhva-app)
summary: A Purāṇa of Śiva-Viṣṇu identity: creation and cosmography, the Pāśupata way, the Īśvara Gītā on yoga and knowledge, the Vyāsa Gītā on dharma, tīrthas and the rites for the dead; it lists the eighteen Mahāpurāṇas and eighteen Upapurāṇas.

title: Matsya Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Spoken by Viṣṇu as the Fish to Manu Vaivasvata at the flood (Matsya 53.5-7).
attribution.scholarly: Among the older Purāṇas, with borrowings from the Vāyu; contains the standard descriptions of the eighteen Purāṇas.

scholarly.text: core c. 3rd-6th c. CE with later additions

structure.description: c. 290 chapters; 14,000 verses by the traditional count

notes: 53: definitions and gift-rules of the eighteen Purāṇas and some Upapurāṇas, the five marks, and the sāttvika/rājasa/tāmasa/saṅkīrṇa classification; later chapters: the sixteen great gifts (mahādāna), iconography (pratimā-lakṣaṇa), Prayāga and Avimukta (Vārāṇasī) māhātmyas. verse number checked in the local e-text of the Matsya Purāṇa (raw_etexts mAdhva-app)
summary: The Fish avatāra's teaching to Manu: creation, manvantaras, genealogies, vows and gifts (the sixteen great gifts), śrāddha, iconography and temple lore, tīrthas, and the authoritative descriptions of all the Purāṇas.

title: Garuḍa Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Spoken by Viṣṇu (Kṛṣṇa) to Garuḍa, then handed down through Kaśyapa and the sages to Vyāsa and the Sūta; 19,000 verses (BhP 12.13.8).
attribution.scholarly: Encyclopedic Ācārakāṇḍa (medicine, gems, astrology, ritual, dharma); the Pretakalpa is a separate, much-used manual on death and the rites for the dead; the Brahmakāṇḍa is a late Mādhva-Vaiṣṇava section on the gradation (tāratamya) of deities.

scholarly.text: core c. 9th-10th c. CE; Pretakalpa and Brahmakāṇḍa later

structure.description: Venkateshwara ed.: Pūrvakhaṇḍa/Ācārakāṇḍa 240 chapters; Uttarakhaṇḍa = Dharmakāṇḍa/Pretakalpa 49 chapters + Brahmakāṇḍa 29 chapters (other editions: Pretakhaṇḍa of 35 chapters)

notes: Ācārakāṇḍa 1.142: the ten avatāras; 1.235-239 (approx.): brahma-jñāna, ātma-jñāna, Gītāsāra, Brahmagītāsāra; Pretakalpa 2.38.5: the seven liberating cities; Brahmakāṇḍa 3.1: its own sāttvika/rājasa/tāmasa grading of the Purāṇas. verse number checked in the GRETIL/Sansknet e-text of the Garuḍa Purāṇa (Venkateshwara ed.; Pretakalpa cited as 2.chapter.verse)
summary: A Vaiṣṇava encyclopedia best known for its Pretakalpa: the process of dying, Yama's messengers, the thumb-sized person, the year-long road to Yama's city past sixteen towns and the Vaitaraṇī river, judgment, the preta state and its signs, and the rites that give the dead a body and join them to the ancestors.

title: Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Proclaimed by Vāyu ('vāyuprokta' in the colophons), the eighteenth Purāṇa, 12,000 verses; the Lalitopākhyāna is its appended Uttarabhāga told by Hayagrīva to Agastya.
attribution.scholarly: Shares its core with the Vāyu Purāṇa; the Lalitopākhyāna is a much later Śākta/Śrīvidyā addition; the Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa also claims a Brahmāṇḍa origin.

scholarly.text: core c. 4th-6th c. CE; Lalitopākhyāna much later

structure.description: four pādas (Prakriyā, Anuṣaṅga, Upodghāta, Upasaṃhāra) in three bhāgas; the 12,000-verse saṃhitā ends at Uttarabhāga ch. 4; Lalitopākhyāna = Uttarabhāga chs. 5-44

notes: chapter checked in the GRETIL e-text of the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Venkateshwara ed.)
summary: A classic Purāṇa of creation, cosmography, time, manvantaras and dynasties (with śrāddha and Paraśurāma narratives), closing with the dissolution and the city of Śiva, to which the Lalitopākhyāna is appended.

title: Śiva Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Originally of twelve saṃhitās and a hundred thousand verses, abridged by Vyāsa into seven saṃhitās of 24,000 verses; counted fourth of the eighteen in VP 3.6.21 and BhP 12.7.23.
attribution.scholarly: A late compilation relative to the Vāyu (which several lists count fourth); the Vāyavīya Saṃhitā may be older than the rest.

scholarly.text: compiled c. 10th-14th c. CE (Vāyavīya possibly earlier)

structure.description: seven saṃhitās (Venkateshwara): Vidyeśvara, Rudra (Sṛṣṭi, Satī, Pārvatī, Kumāra, Yuddha khaṇḍas), Śatarudra, Koṭirudra, Umā, Kailāsa, Vāyavīya (pūrva and uttara); 24,000 verses

notes: Vidyeśvara: śravaṇa-kīrtana-manana, liṅga worship, the name, bhasma, rudrākṣa; Koṭirudra: the twelve jyotirliṅgas and the Śivarātri hunter; Umā: hells and Yama's road (not checked); Kailāsa: praṇava and sannyāsa; Vāyavīya: Upamanyu's teaching to Kṛṣṇa - dīkṣā, pañcākṣara (7.2.12-13), yoga (7.2.37-39). verse number checked in the GRETIL e-text of the Śiva Purāṇa books 1 and 7 (Venkateshwara ed.)
summary: The great Śaiva Purāṇa: Śiva as niṣkala (worshipped in the liṅga) and sakala (in the image); the means of hearing, singing and reflecting; the liṅga of fire; Satī and Pārvatī; the jyotirliṅgas; the pañcākṣara and Śaiva initiation; and Upamanyu's five kinds of yoga, their obstacles and powers.

title: Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Vyāsa's Bhāgavata of the Goddess; Śākta tradition counts it as the Mahāpurāṇa 'Bhāgavata' of the lists, the Viṣṇu Bhāgavata being an Upapurāṇa (see dsp:which-bhagavata-is-the-mahapurana); told to Janamejaya.
attribution.scholarly: A Śākta Purāṇa usually treated as an Upapurāṇa by modern scholars; draws on the Brahmavaivarta (Book 9) and the Devī Māhātmya.

structure.description: 12 skandhas, 318 chapters, c. 18,000 verses

notes: Devī Gītā = Skandha 7 chs. 31-40 (U06/U23 own src:devi-gita); Maṇidvīpa = Skandha 12 chs. 10-12; Navarātra vow in Skandha 3; Skandha 9 parallels the Brahmavaivarta's Prakṛti-khaṇḍa. No local e-text: chapter locators from memory (moderate/low).
summary: The Goddess as the supreme Brahman and Mother of the Trimūrti: her revelation to Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva in Maṇidvīpa, her avatāras and battles, the Navarātra vow, Prakṛti's forms, the Devī Gītā on yoga and knowledge, sadācāra and Gāyatrī, and the description of her island-paradise Maṇidvīpa.

title: Devī Māhātmya

attribution.tradition: The sage Medhas tells the deposed king Suratha and the merchant Samādhi the glory of the Goddess Mahāmāyā; Mārkaṇḍeya relates it as the account of the eighth Manu, Sāvarṇi.
attribution.scholarly: The earliest text to present the Goddess as the supreme reality; inserted into the Mārkaṇḍeya.

structure.description: 13 chapters in three caritas (ch. 1; chs. 2-4; chs. 5-13). The tradition counts 700 mantras (hence 'Saptaśatī') by counting half-verses, speaker-lines and refrains; the metrical verses number c. 580-590 (588 numbered verses in the Sansknet e-text)

notes: Recited with ancillary texts (aṅgas): Kavaca, Argalā, Kīlaka before, and the three Rahasyas (Prādhānika, Vaikṛtika, Mūrti) after; the naming of the three caritas' deities as Mahākālī, Mahālakṣmī and Mahāsarasvatī comes from the dhyāna verses and the Rahasyas, not from the 13 chapters themselves. Commentaries include Bhāskararāya's Guptavatī (src:guptavati) and the Śāntanavī. Śākta theology shared with U23. verse number checked in the GRETIL/Sansknet e-text of the MkP (chs. 1-93; Devī Māhātmya = MkP 81-93 in this numbering)
summary: The Goddess, Mahāmāyā, is the eternal source and power of the world who deludes even the wise and grants liberation; she wakes Viṣṇu to slay Madhu and Kaiṭabha, arises from the gods' combined radiance to slay Mahiṣa, and as Ambikā with Kālī/Cāmuṇḍā and the Mothers slays Śumbha, Niśumbha and their generals; hymned as present in all beings ('yā devī sarvabhūteṣu'), she promises to return whenever demons oppress the world.

title: Lalitopākhyāna

attribution.tradition: Hayagrīva, a portion of Viṣṇu, teaches Agastya the story and worship of Lalitā (Tripurasundarī).
attribution.scholarly: A late Śrīvidyā text appended to the Brahmāṇḍa.

structure.description: 40 chapters (Uttarabhāga 5-44)

notes: The Lalitā Sahasranāma and Triśatī (U23) name the Brahmāṇḍa's Uttarakhaṇḍa (Hayagrīva-Agastya dialogue) as their source, but their texts are not contained in the printed Lalitopākhyāna (checked: no sahasranāma in the local e-text). chapter checked in the GRETIL e-text of the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Venkateshwara ed.)
summary: Lalitā arises from the fire-altar of the gods' sacrifice to destroy Bhaṇḍāsura, the demon born from the ashes of Kāma burnt by Śiva; the war of her śaktis, her city Śrīpura, her union with Kāmeśvara and the revival of Kāma; with the worship of the Goddess.

title: Garuḍa Purāṇa, Pretakalpa

attribution.tradition: Kṛṣṇa's answers to Garuḍa's questions on the fate of the dead (with a Bhīṣma-Yudhiṣṭhira dialogue in ch. 22).
attribution.scholarly: A manual of death and the rites for the dead; recensions differ in chapter count (35 in some editions).

structure.description: 49 chapters (Venkateshwara)

notes: Chapter topics (from the colophons of the local e-text): 1 questions; 2 after-death rites and karmic results; 3 hells; 4 cremation, deaths in pañcaka; 5 annual rites and the road to Yama; 6 vṛṣotsarga; 7 five pretas; 8 self-śrāddha; 11 the openings of departure; 12 only dharma follows the dead; 14 gifts; 15 Yama's world; 16 the preta's journey; 19 entry into Yama's hall and new bodies; 20-23 the abode, harassment, dreams and signs of pretas and their release; 24-25 untimely deaths and children; 26 sapiṇḍana; 27 Babhruvāhana and the preta; 32 embryology; 36 death by fasting; 38 higher worlds and liberation; 39 impurity periods; 44 bad deaths; 45 annual śrāddha; 46-48 destinies and karma; 49 means of liberation. verse number checked in the GRETIL/Sansknet e-text of the Garuḍa Purāṇa (Venkateshwara ed.; Pretakalpa cited as 2.chapter.verse)
summary: The classical Purāṇic manual of dying and the afterlife: the signs and pains of death, the thumb-sized person led off by Yama's messengers, the airy conveyance-body and the body built by the ten days' piṇḍas, the year-long road, the Vaitaraṇī, judgment, the preta state and its release through the sons' rites, gifts to the dying, and the means of liberation.

title: Garuḍa Purāṇa Sāroddhāra

attribution.tradition: The 'extracted essence' of the Garuḍa's teaching on the dead, read aloud in households during the days of mourning.
attribution.scholarly: A later compilation of 16 chapters from the Pretakalpa ascribed to Navanidhirāma (Naunidhirāma); translated by E. Wood and S. V. Subrahmanyam (1911).

structure.description: 16 chapters

notes: Compiler's name and date not verified - low confidence; kept as the text actually recited in mourning in North India.
summary: A sixteen-chapter digest of the Garuḍa's teaching on death: the miseries of sinners, the road and city of Yama, the hells, rebirth and embryonic suffering, gifts and rites at death, the ten days, sapiṇḍīkaraṇa, and the conduct that leads to heaven or liberation.

title: Vāyavīya Saṃhitā

attribution.tradition: Vāyu tells the sages of Naimiṣa; within it Upamanyu instructs Kṛṣṇa in Śaiva initiation, worship, the pañcākṣara and yoga.
attribution.scholarly: Possibly the oldest stratum of the Śiva Purāṇa, close to the Pāśupata and Siddhānta traditions.

structure.description: Pūrvakhaṇḍa 35 chapters, Uttarakhaṇḍa 41 chapters (Venkateshwara)

notes: verse number checked in the GRETIL e-text of the Śiva Purāṇa books 1 and 7 (Venkateshwara ed.)
summary: Śaiva theology of Śiva and Śakti, Pāśupata vow, Upamanyu's teaching to Kṛṣṇa on dīkṣā and the six paths, the pañcākṣara, daily and occasional worship, and yoga in five kinds with eight or six limbs, its obstacles and powers, and meditation with and without object.

title: Kāśī Khaṇḍa

attribution.tradition: Skanda's account of Kāśī (Vārāṇasī); opens with Agastya and Lopāmudrā's pilgrimage and their dialogue on tīrthas.
attribution.scholarly: A major Vārāṇasī māhātmya, commonly dated to the early 2nd millennium CE.

notes: 6.28-45 on inner tīrthas checked in the local e-text (numbered 4.1.6.30 etc.).
summary: The glory of Kāśī where death brings liberation, its liṅgas and tīrthas, and the teaching that the supreme tīrtha is purity of mind.

title: Sūta Saṃhitā
location_in_parent: one of the six saṃhitās of the Skanda (saṃhitā arrangement)

attribution.tradition: The Sūta's saṃhitā of the Skanda; commented on by Mādhavācārya (Vidyāraṇya) in the Tātparyadīpikā.
attribution.scholarly: A Śaiva non-dualist text valued by Advaitins; contains the Brahma Gītā and Sūta Gītā in its Yajñavaibhava-khaṇḍa.

summary: Śaiva Advaita: Śiva as the non-dual self, the path of knowledge and Śaiva worship, with the Brahma Gītā and Sūta Gītā.

title: Skandapurāṇa (early recension)

attribution.tradition: Skanda's Purāṇa as preserved in Nepal.
attribution.scholarly: A distinct early Śaiva Purāṇa preserved in Nepalese palm-leaf manuscripts, the oldest dated 810 CE; critical edition in progress (Groningen: Adriaensen, Bakker, Isaacson and others).

notes: Distinct from the printed Skanda Mahāpurāṇa; strong Pāśupata and Vārāṇasī content.
summary: Śiva's myths (Pārvatī, Skanda's birth, the destruction of Andhaka), the Vārāṇasī māhātmya and early Pāśupata religion, in a text far older than the printed Skanda.

title: Bhāgavata Māhātmya
location_in_parent: Uttarakhaṇḍa (six chapters); another version in the Skanda Vaiṣṇavakhaṇḍa

attribution.tradition: Prefixed to printed Bhāgavatas; Sanaka and the Kumāras teach Nārada the seven-day hearing (saptāha) of the Bhāgavata.
attribution.scholarly: Late (probably 2nd millennium CE).

notes: Colophons 'śrīpadmapurāṇe uttarakhaṇḍe śrīmadbhāgavatamāhātmye' checked in the local e-text (BhP wiki 00).
summary: Bhakti, with her sons Knowledge and Detachment grown old in the Kali age, is revived by the Bhāgavata; the seven-day hearing surpasses sacrifice, vows, yoga and meditation; the preta Dhundhukārī is freed by hearing it from his brother Gokarṇa.

title: Harivaṃśa

attribution.tradition: Vaiśampāyana's continuation to Janamejaya of the Mahābhārata, on the lineage of Hari.
attribution.scholarly: The earliest connected account of Kṛṣṇa's childhood and life; in form a Purāṇa (creation, genealogies).

structure.description: critical edition 118 chapters with appendices; vulgate in three parvans (Harivaṃśa, Viṣṇu, Bhaviṣya)

summary: Creation and the dynasties, then Kṛṣṇa's birth, childhood in Vraja (including the hallīsaka dance with the cowherd women), deeds at Mathurā and Dvārakā; the Purāṇic life of Kṛṣṇa that the Viṣṇu and Bhāgavata Purāṇas expand.

title: Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: An Upapurāṇa (a supplement to the Viṣṇudharma).
attribution.scholarly: Kashmiri Vaiṣṇava encyclopedia; famous for its Citrasūtra on painting and its chapters on image-making, music, dance and poetics.

structure.description: three khaṇḍas

summary: A Vaiṣṇava encyclopedia of cosmology, dharma, astronomy and the arts (the Citrasūtra), with Pāñcarātra-coloured worship.

title: Viṣṇudharma

attribution.tradition: Dialogues on Vaiṣṇava dharma.
attribution.scholarly: An early Vaiṣṇava dharma text (critically edited by R. Grünendahl).

summary: Vaiṣṇava lay dharma: vows, worship of Vāsudeva, merit and its fruits.

title: Narasiṃha Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Listed second among the Upapurāṇas (KūP 1.1.17); 18,000 verses by Matsya 53.60.
attribution.scholarly: A Vaiṣṇava Upapurāṇa with the Narasiṃha and Prahlāda narratives.

summary: Narasiṃha and Prahlāda, the avatāras, creation, and Vaiṣṇava worship and yoga.

title: Kālikā Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Listed among the eighteen Upapurāṇas (KūP 1.1.19).
attribution.scholarly: A Śākta Upapurāṇa of Kāmarūpa (Assam), central to Kāmākhyā worship (U24 owns the Śākta detail).

summary: The Goddess's worship at Kāmākhyā, Satī's body and the pīṭhas, Śākta rites (including blood offering), and the sacred geography of Kāmarūpa.

title: Devī Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: A Purāṇa of the Goddess.
attribution.scholarly: An early Śākta Upapurāṇa of eastern India.

summary: The Goddess's battles and worship, vows and festivals, with early tantric ritual.

title: Mahābhāgavata Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: The 'great Bhāgavata' of the Goddess.
attribution.scholarly: A Bengal Śākta Upapurāṇa; contains the Bhagavatī (Pārvatī) Gītā.

summary: The Goddess as supreme; Satī and the ten Mahāvidyās; the Bhagavatī Gītā on devotion and knowledge.

title: Bṛhaddharma Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: An Upapurāṇa.
attribution.scholarly: A Bengal Upapurāṇa, important for Bengali caste and ritual history.

summary: Dharma, Gaṅgā-māhātmya, the Goddess and the ordering of castes in Bengal.

title: Gaṇeśa Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: The Purāṇa of Gaṇeśa; contains the Gaṇeśa Gītā (U06).
attribution.scholarly: A Gāṇapatya Upapurāṇa.

summary: Gaṇeśa as the supreme Brahman, his avatāras in the four ages, vows and worship, and the Gaṇeśa Gītā.

title: Mudgala Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: A Purāṇa of Gaṇeśa told by the sage Mudgala.
attribution.scholarly: A Gāṇapatya Upapurāṇa teaching eight incarnations of Gaṇeśa against eight vices.

summary: Eight forms of Gaṇeśa, each overcoming a demon that embodies a vice, and Gāṇapatya yoga.

title: Sāmba Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Listed among the Upapurāṇas (KūP 1.1.20; Matsya 53.62).
attribution.scholarly: A Saura Upapurāṇa: Kṛṣṇa's son Sāmba, cured of leprosy by the Sun, brings the Maga priests.

summary: The worship of Sūrya, Sāmba's cure and the Maga priests; solar images and temples.

title: Saura Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Listed among the Upapurāṇas (KūP 1.1.20).
attribution.scholarly: Despite the name, a Śaiva Upapurāṇa (told by Sūrya), with Śaiva theology.

summary: Śiva worship taught by the Sun; Śaiva doctrine and vows.

title: Kapila Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Listed among the Upapurāṇas (KūP 1.1.19).
attribution.scholarly: A minor Upapurāṇa (local e-text exists).

summary: A minor Upapurāṇa of tīrthas and dharma.

title: Nīlamata Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: The teaching of the Nāga king Nīla on the rites of Kashmir.
attribution.scholarly: A Kashmiri text of local festivals and cults, used by Kalhaṇa.

summary: The origin of the Kashmir valley from the lake Satīsaras, and the Nāgas' rites and seasonal festivals of Kashmir.

title: Parāśara Upapurāṇa

attribution.tradition: 'Spoken by Parāśara' (KūP 1.1.20).
attribution.scholarly: A minor Upapurāṇa (local e-text exists).

summary: An Upapurāṇa attributed to Parāśara on dharma and worship.

title: Kalki Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: The future avatāra Kalki.
attribution.scholarly: A late Upapurāṇa.

summary: The birth and deeds of Kalki at the end of the Kali age, the destruction of the wicked and the return of the Kṛta age.

title: Śivadharma

attribution.tradition: The fourth Upapurāṇa, 'spoken by Nandīśa' (KūP 1.1.18).
attribution.scholarly: The earliest Śaiva text of lay religion, preserved in Nepal, with its sequel the Śivadharmottara.

summary: The dharma of lay Śaiva devotees: liṅga worship, gifts to Śaiva ascetics, vows, the building of temples and the rewards in Śiva's worlds.

title: Śivadharmottara

attribution.tradition: Sequel to the Śivadharma.
attribution.scholarly: Early Śaiva lay dharma, with the gift of knowledge (vidyādāna) and the Śaiva hells and heavens.

summary: The gift of Śaiva scripture, Śaiva teachers, and the fruits of Śaiva dharma in the worlds after death.

title: Bhaviṣyottara Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Kṛṣṇa's instruction to Yudhiṣṭhira on vows.
attribution.scholarly: A major source of vrata-kathās.

summary: Vows (vratas) of the lunar year, their stories, rules and fruits.

title: Bṛhannāradīya Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: An Upapurāṇa of Nārada.
attribution.scholarly: Distinguished by scholars from the Nāradīya Mahāpurāṇa; strongly Vaiṣṇava, with the praise of the name 'harer nāma'.

notes: The verse 'harer nāma harer nāma harer nāmaiva kevalam / kalau nāsty eva nāsty eva nāsty eva gatir anyathā' is attributed to the Bṛhannāradīya by Gauḍīya authors; location not checked.
summary: Vaiṣṇava devotion and the power of Hari's name in the Kali age.

title: Sanatkumāra Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: The first Upapurāṇa in the Kūrma's list (KūP 1.1.17).
attribution.scholarly: Status of any surviving text uncertain.

summary: Listed as the first Upapurāṇa, 'spoken by Sanatkumāra'; no surviving text confirmed in this sweep.

title: Āditya Purāṇa

attribution.tradition: Named with the Upapurāṇas (Matsya 53.63).
attribution.scholarly: Known mainly from quotations in digests.

summary: An Upapurāṇa named in the lists and quoted in digests; no complete text confirmed.

title: Bhāvārthadīpikā

attribution.tradition: Śrīdhara Svāmin's gloss; the Gauḍīya biographies report Caitanya's insistence on following it.
attribution.scholarly: The most widely used commentary on the Bhāgavata, non-dualist yet devotional.

summary: A concise commentary reading the Bhāgavata as non-dual Vedānta culminating in devotion to Bhagavān.

title: Ātmaprakāśa

attribution.tradition: Śrīdhara's commentary on the Viṣṇu Purāṇa.
attribution.scholarly: Printed with the Viṣṇucittīya.

notes: Named in the heading of the local e-text ('viṣṇucittyātmaprakāśākhyaśrīdharīya vyākhyādvayopetam').
summary: Śrīdhara's gloss on the Viṣṇu Purāṇa.

title: Viṣṇucittīya

attribution.tradition: Viṣṇucitta's Śrīvaiṣṇava commentary on the Viṣṇu Purāṇa.
attribution.scholarly: A Viśiṣṭādvaita reading of the VP, which Rāmānuja had cited heavily.

notes: Named in the heading of the local e-text.
summary: A Viśiṣṭādvaita commentary on the Viṣṇu Purāṇa.

title: Guptavatī

attribution.tradition: Bhāskararāya's commentary on the Saptaśatī.
attribution.scholarly: An 18th-c. Śrīvidyā reading of the Devī Māhātmya.

summary: A Śrīvidyā commentary on the Devī Māhātmya, with its mantra-structure and recitation.

title: Prādhānika Rahasya

attribution.tradition: The first of the three 'secrets' (rahasya-traya) recited after the Saptaśatī.
attribution.scholarly: Later ancillary text.

summary: The primordial Mahālakṣmī, source of Mahākālī and Mahāsarasvatī, and through them of the divine couples - the theology behind the three forms of the Saptaśatī's caritas.

title: Kṛtyakalpataru

attribution.tradition: Lakṣmīdhara's digest of dharma.
attribution.scholarly: A 12th-c. digest (Gāhaḍavāla court) whose volumes on vratas, dāna, tīrthas and śrāddha are built largely from Purāṇic quotations.

summary: A digest of dharma in fourteen books, preserving Purāṇic teaching on vows, gifts, pilgrimage, śrāddha and liberation.

title: Caturvargacintāmaṇi

attribution.tradition: Hemādri's 'wish-gem of the four aims'.
attribution.scholarly: A 13th-c. Yādava-court digest; its Vrata-khaṇḍa and Dāna-khaṇḍa collect Purāṇic vrata and dāna teaching.

summary: An encyclopedic digest of vows, gifts, times and rites, drawn largely from the Purāṇas.
